the evaluation of large-scale EHR implementations should adopt an approach which moves away from the conventional model of baseline operations, intervention, changed operations, and outcome, and instead account for the changing contexts of these implementations.
the evaluation of EHR implementations is challenging because of the shifting sand of evolving sociopolitics and sociotechnical contexts, which must be accounted for in evaluations of such endeavors.

the implementation and adoption, not just of a particular EHR system, but of a national policy and strategy for EHRs.
how to build the foundations of an EHR system on shifting sands, and how to evaluate its progress.

The main takeaway from our work is that

evaluation needs to move from an assumption that there is a stable and fixed ‘baseline’ to one where the baseline is constantly changing and evolving, and where evaluation must be responsive and adaptive to these changes.

the evaluation of national EHR implementations should take into account the changing context of the implementation and the multiple perspectives on the implementation, and should therefore be based on interpretive approaches.

evaluations of national EHR implementation programs should be designed in such a way that they can adapt to changing contexts and that the evaluation itself is seen as a process that evolves over time.
